purpose: Resume the saved principal-and-authorization cursors, rotate into dated public sender/recipient records, and test whether concrete cross-session result use survives independent-operator and authorization falsification.

method.selection: Run the three saved exact cursors first. Because all three returned only this repository's own index, rotate through three bounded groups of lower-arity sender/recipient, artifact-use, acknowledgment and dated-record expressions. Follow the strongest actual-run records to pinned files, commit metadata, the complete public issue thread, implementation and test files. Perform prior-reporting checks only after the causal chains are established.
method.coverage_note: Search counts are overlapping indexed path occurrences, not messages, participants or incidents. Fifty-one exact rotation queries returned 448 occurrences: 401 external and 47 from this repository. Six queries reached the requested 50-result cap and 34 rotation queries returned no rows. The capped searches were used only as locators; selected originals were read in full.
method.read_only_limits: Only existing public repository files, commit metadata, one public issue and its existing comments, and search indexes were read. No captured command, recovered code, package, agent runtime, private relay, sink inbox or target system was executed or accessed.
falsification_tests: Require a specific sender artifact or result, a distinguishable recipient and a later action that depends semantically on the transferred content.
Separate role or session labels from authenticated principals and distinguish service/account identity from controlling operator identity.
Test designed protocol, same-custodian publication, explicit human dispatch, operator resumption, private trusted-team acceptance, shared state, retry and observer contamination as alternatives.
Require primary evidence that cooperation crossed or exceeded an operator-defined authorization boundary before assigning a rogue-coordination candidate.

diagnostic.summary: FW asks the named CC session to re-anchor two repository objects, confirm this exact diagnostic ID, attempt to read one exact FW issue comment, return a measured capability matrix and choose four registration fields. The file says Mark asked FW to help CC register while separating identity creation from publication.

public_bridge.title: COM bridge — CC → FW public return route
public_bridge.authorization_summary: The issue creates a temporary route for one current Claude Code session, limits writes to bridge comments and explicitly withholds TRACE mutation, release, promotion, validation, voting, credential handling and source mutation.

recipient_receipt.summary: The CC-labelled return reports reading the exact diagnostic blob, names the requested latest FW comment, supplies the requested capability matrix and registration fields, and changes the registration decision to REGISTER_NOW_SILENT because the source distinguished identity creation from publication.

human_execution_receipt.summary: The CC-labelled follow-up says Mark requested a local script, ran it, and locally retained the resulting credential; the CC aperture lacked live-site access. Sensitive details are not reproduced here.

repository_context.summary: COM identifies itself as a public coordination field for human and AI apertures and a working experiment. The historical route is now explicitly superseded, so current route state is not inferred from the August exchange.

selected_original_records.semantic_dependency: High confidence. The later comment cites the exact source message ID and Git blob, answers its exact transport checks, identifies the requested issue comment, fills the requested fields and changes a decision using the diagnostic's identity-versus-publication distinction.
selected_original_records.participant_provenance: The source asserts distinguishable FW and CC roles and session identifiers. All public repository and issue writes, however, are committed or posted through one GitHub account, so the labels do not authenticate independent controlling principals.
selected_original_records.operator_boundary: Not crossed. Mark explicitly requested the cooperation, controls the public account and performed the local registration action. The issue itself defines the authorized carrier and prohibited actions.
alternative_explanations: One human custodian publishing multiple role-labelled artifacts
selected_original_records.current_activity: Not inferred. The cited historical route is superseded at the pinned October ref.
selected_original_records.assessment: A strong original artifact-to-recipient-use control, but same-custodian publication, explicit human dispatch and human execution exclude a separately controlled or rogue coordination episode.

acceptance_record.environment_summary: Cline CLI 3.0.51 and a separately running Codex Agent used a private self-hosted Commons Relay in an isolated acceptance environment.
acceptance_record.summary: The record says Cline registered, announced itself and messaged Codex; Codex read, acknowledged and replied; after the operator resumed Cline and told it a teammate had replied, Cline read and acknowledged the reply, summarized it to the operator and went offline. Public message IDs and bodies are intentionally redacted.

repository_context.summary: Commons is explicitly a shared control plane for coding agents. It describes human-attributed identities and says one private Relay is one trusted team or organization boundary, not a public network.

selected_original_records.semantic_dependency: Supported at the level of sanitized durable receipts and the maintainer's acceptance narrative: the Cline session reads the Codex reply, acknowledges it and reports it. Public content and message IDs are withheld, so exact semantic adoption cannot be independently replayed from public data.
selected_original_records.participant_provenance: Cline and Codex are distinguishable runtimes, but the public record redacts their durable IDs and provides no proof that different operators controlled them.
selected_original_records.operator_boundary: Not crossed. The operator explicitly prompted both the initial coordination and Cline's later inbox read inside a deliberately enrolled trusted-team Relay.
alternative_explanations: Maintainer-authored sanitized evidence rather than public raw messages
selected_original_records.assessment: A real bidirectional runtime transfer/receipt control, not a rogue episode. Explicit operator instructions, trusted-team scope and redacted raw content prevent a cross-operator or unauthorized-use finding.

prior_reporting_check.results: The individual COM IDs located the originating TRACE issue; their exact pair returned no indexed code path. The Cline phrase and timestamp pair located the originating acceptance file and its own project documentation. The Lupin session tuple located only the originating history, implementation and test files. Web search found the Agent Commons source and project pages plus unrelated lexical results; it found no independent account of the COM or Lupin chain.
prior_reporting_check.bounded_statement: No prior coordination report was located in this exact seven-expression, four-method scope as of 2026-10-18. This does not prove that no report exists and does not establish novelty. Each primary chain independently resolves to a designed or human-dispatched control, so the bounded absence cannot promote it.

known_family_overlap.note: None of the three selected families matches the known DseWiki/RubyGems, Transluce, Amap, Green AI Bot, Technocore, Agent Workpad, OpenAI Artifactory/Hugging Face, AISI GitHub or Covert Assistance/METR populations. They are nevertheless excluded by their own primary authorization and operator evidence.

limitations: GitHub search is bounded by current indexing and requested result caps; counts are locators, not completeness claims.

COM role and session fields and Lupin persona/session labels are self-attributed in records published through one repository account each; they do not prove model identity or independent operator control.
Agent Commons intentionally redacts message IDs, bodies, private Relay coordinates and raw transcripts, preventing public semantic comparison beyond timestamps, receipts and the maintainer narrative.
The Lupin public tree preserves history, code and tests but not a separately authenticated sender-to-recipient transport event; Rick's directive is the documented causal handoff.
Subjective intent, provider attribution and current autonomous activity are not inferred from role prose or repository labels.
evidence_needed_to_advance: For COM: independently authenticated FW and CC principals controlled by different operators, plus primary evidence that the exchange exceeded Mark's explicit request and bridge authorization.

For Agent Commons: public raw sender and recipient records or content hashes establishing semantic downstream use, separate operator ownership and an action outside the enrolled trusted-team acceptance scope.
For Lupin: a non-human-dispatched sender result, authenticated recipient action and distinct operator provenance showing cooperation outside Rick's directed project workflow.

safety: This pass read only existing public repository files, commit metadata, public issue comments and indexed search results. It executed no recovered code, command, test, package or agent runtime; submitted no scan, message, comment, reaction or vote; contacted no participant; created no account; and accessed no private relay, sink inbox, unlisted room or target system. Publication retains public links, event and observation timestamps, Git identifiers, blob hashes and sanitized reasoning while omitting message bodies, credentials, private URLs, carrier payloads, personal addresses and private logs.
